transcript:
Mira: The community center is our venue for Friday evening. Can we finish the programme before we invite the first guest?

Cal: Yes. This festival brings the community together. The celebration starts at six, and admission is two dollars for the room costs. The ticket notice should say that clearly before anyone pays.

Mira: How many people can sit in the audience? I heard someone mention eighty, but I do not want to print the wrong number.

Cal: The room has thirty seats, not eighty. A crowd can make the entrance difficult to use, so we will ask people to sign up in advance.

Mira: The band wants a rehearsal on Thursday at four. Will the stage be free then, or is another group using it?

Cal: The stage is being cleaned until three, so four is fine. The microphone will be checked before the singer arrives. We should tell every performer where to wait.

Mira: Who is bringing an instrument? I know Lena has a violin, but I have not heard about the others.

Cal: Lena has the violin, and Omar is bringing a guitar. I will bring a small drum for the rhythm. The center already has a piano, so nobody needs to move one.

Mira: Good. We will play one song together, then ask the guest to speak. Can you announce the order at the beginning of the concert?

Cal: I can. I will also check the invitation before we print it. The start time and cost need to be visible, and the guest needs a clear route to the room.

Mira: My sister is making a banner and paper stars. A child has a costume for the story. My sister wants to decorate the entrance, but she asked whether there will be a parade outside.

Cal: No parade is planned for this event. After the music, the audience can applaud. We will follow the applause with a short break and invite everyone to a conversation in the room. Anyone who needs to leave may do so quietly.
